questions.question: What is the Trickle-Down Theory of fashion? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the Trickle-Down Theory of fashion?
  • The trickle-down theory states that fashion trends start from the upper class or elite groups
  • and are later adopted by the middle and lower classes. Once lower groups begin wearing the
  • style, the elite move on to new fashions to maintain distinction.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write two factors affecting the length of fashion cycle. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Write two factors affecting the length of fashion cycle.
  • The fashion cycle is influenced by the buying power of consumers, which determines how
  • quickly they adopt or reject styles, and social or cultural changes, which can speed up or slow
  • down the popularity of a trend.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Define fashion business. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define fashion business.
  • Fashion business is the industry involved in designing, producing, marketing, and selling
  • apparel, accessories, and footwear. It combines creative design with commercial operations to
  • deliver fashion products to consumers.

questions.question: Name any two core components of the Mordern Fashion Business. / [CO4] [2x10 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Name any two core components of the Modern Fashion Business.
  • Two important core components of modern fashion business are design and production, and
  • marketing and merchandising. Design and production involve creating the garment, choosing
  • fabrics, developing patterns, and manufacturing the final product. Marketing and
  • merchandising focus on understanding consumer needs, planning collections, promoting
  • products, and ensuring they reach the right customers at the right time. Together, these
  • components help brands create attractive products and successfully sell them in the market.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe the features of fad fashion. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the features of fad fashion.
  • Fad fashion refers to styles that become popular very quickly and disappear just as fast. These
  • fashions attract attention mainly because they are new, unique, or eye-catching. Fads spread
  • rapidly among the youth due to media, influencers, and peer groups. Their life span is
  • extremely short—sometimes only a few weeks or months—because they lack long-lasting
  • design value. Once consumer excitement fades, the fad disappears and is replaced by another
  • temporary trend.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write short notes on reverse adaptation with examples. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Write short notes on reverse adaptation with examples.
  • Reverse adaptation, also known as the trickle-up theory, explains how fashion trends start
  • among lower-income groups or street culture and gradually move upward to high fashion.
  • Instead of designers introducing new styles first, everyday people such as workers, youth, and
  • subcultures influence the fashion industry. Designers adopt these styles, modify them, and
  • present them on runways. Examples include jeans, which began as workwear for miners and
  • later became worldwide fashion, and streetwear styles like hoodies and sneakers that have
  • been adopted by luxury brands.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the concept of pret-a-porter in fashion. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the concept of prêt-à-porter in fashion.
  • Prêt-à-porter, or ready-to-wear, refers to clothing produced in standardized sizes and sold in a
  • finished condition. These garments are manufactured in large quantities, making them more
  • affordable and accessible than haute couture. Ready-to-wear collections are showcased
  • during fashion weeks for each season and are available immediately in stores. They aim to
  • balance designer creativity with practicality, offering fashionable clothing that can be worn
  • without alterations.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe the role of supplier and manufacturer in fashion business. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role of supplier and manufacturer in fashion business.
  • Suppliers and manufacturers play key roles in the fashion industry. Suppliers provide raw
  • materials such as fabrics, trims, buttons, zippers, and threads, and ensure that materials meet
  • quality standards and delivery timelines. Manufacturers convert these materials into finished
  • garments through cutting, sewing, assembling, and finishing. They maintain size accuracy,
  • quality control, and production deadlines. Both are essential for smooth, efficient garment
  • production.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Mention any four categories of kid’s wear with suitable examples. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Mention any four categories of kid’s wear with suitable examples.
  • Kids’ wear includes several categories based on age and needs. Babywear consists of onesies
  • and rompers designed for newborn comfort. Boys’ wear includes shirts, jeans, T-shirts, and
  • shorts suitable for daily activities. Girls’ wear offers dresses, skirts, leggings, and tunics that
  • are comfortable and stylish. School uniforms include shirts, pants, skirts, and pinafores worn
  • by children in educational institutions. These categories focus on safety, comfort, and
  • practicality.

questions.question: Explain how trend forecasting differs from fashion forecasting. Provide examples of industries involved in each. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how trend forecasting differs from fashion forecasting. Provide
  • examples.
  • Trend forecasting is a broad study of consumer behavior, cultural changes, and lifestyle
  • patterns across various industries such as food, technology, interiors, and fashion. It predicts
  • long-term societal movements. Fashion forecasting, however, focuses specifically on
  • predicting future clothing trends such as colors, fabrics, silhouettes, and textures for
  • upcoming seasons. For example, a trend forecast may identify rising concern for
  • sustainability, while a fashion forecast may predict natural tones and organic fabrics as
  • upcoming fashion trends.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe how Trade fairs help in gathering forecasting information. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how Trade fairs help in gathering forecasting information.
  • Trade fairs help gather forecasting information by introducing new fabrics, colors, textures,
  • and technological innovations. Designers and buyers attend these fairs to observe what
  • suppliers and manufacturers are offering for future seasons. Trade fairs allow brands to
  • understand upcoming market directions, assessment of consumer interest, and insights into
  • competitor strategies. This helps companies in planning collections and staying updated with
  • industry trends.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe two ways in which forecasting improves coordination and control. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe two ways in which forecasting improves coordination and
  • control.
  • Forecasting improves coordination by ensuring all departments—design, production, and
  • marketing—work according to the same future plan, reducing confusion and improving
  • teamwork. It improves control by helping businesses plan materials, manage inventory, and
  • schedule production efficiently. Accurate forecasting prevents wastage, overproduction, and
  • financial loss.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is Research & Observation, Data Collection and Validation in Fashion Forecasting Framework? / [CO3] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• What is Research & Observation, Data Collection and Validation in
  • Fashion Forecasting Framework?
  • Research and observation involve studying culture, lifestyles, street fashion, and social
  • influences to identify emerging trends. Data collection gathers information through surveys,
  • interviews, fashion shows, magazines, and sales records. Validation checks whether
  • predictions are correct by testing sample garments, collecting feedback, and making
  • adjustments before final decisions. These steps ensure reliable forecasting.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain how understanding fashion cycle stages helps fashion marketers and designers. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how understanding fashion cycle stages helps fashion marketers
  • and designers.
  • Understanding the five stages of the fashion cycle—introduction, rise, peak, decline, and
  • rejection—is essential for both marketers and designers. During the introduction stage,
  • designers release new styles and marketers target early adopters. As the style gains popularity
  • in the rise stage, production increases and promotional activities expand. At the peak stage,
  • the trend becomes widely accepted, so marketers use strong advertising while designers may
  • introduce variations to extend interest. In the decline stage, demand decreases and marketers
  • shift to discounting strategies. During the rejection stage, the style becomes outdated,
  • requiring retailers to clear old stock and designers to introduce fresh styles. This
  • understanding helps brands plan production, pricing, inventory, and marketing strategies
  • effectively.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Discuss the various categories of women's wear with examples. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the various categories of women’s wear with examples.
  • Women’s wear includes a wide range of clothing for various occasions. Tops include shirts,
  • tunics, blouses, and crop tops suitable for casual and formal use. Bottoms such as trousers,
  • skirts, jeans, leggings, and palazzos offer comfort and versatility. Dresses including maxi, A-
  • line, and cocktail styles are worn for parties, work, and casual outings. Ethnic wear like
  • sarees, salwar suits, lehengas, and anarkalis is preferred for festivals and traditional events.
  • Outerwear such as coats, jackets, and blazers provide warmth and style. Lingerie and
  • nightwear ensure comfort, while sportswear like yoga pants and active tops support fitness
  • activities. Accessories such as scarves, handbags, and jewellery enhance the overall outfit.

questions.question: Explain the two main types of fashion forecasting – long-term and short-term. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the two main types of fashion forecasting – long-term and short-
  • term.
  • Long-term forecasting predicts major cultural, social, technological, and economic shifts that
  • influence fashion over two to five years. It focuses on broad trends such as sustainability,
  • lifestyle changes, and technological innovations. Brands use long-term forecasts for planning
  • strategy, market positioning, and fabric development. Short-term forecasting focuses on
  • details like colors, fabrics, textures, prints, and silhouettes for the upcoming six to eighteen
  • months. It relies on fashion shows, trade fairs, street style, and celebrity influence. Designers
  • use short-term forecasts for creating seasonal collections. Both forecasting types together
  • help brands create successful products.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe the various methods of promotion used by fashion companies to attract and retain customers. / [CO4] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the various methods of promotion used by fashion companies to
  • attract and retain customers.
  • Fashion companies use several promotional methods to increase visibility and sales.
  • Advertising through magazines, television, social media, and billboards helps reach large
  • audiences. Sales promotions such as discounts, seasonal offers, and coupons attract
  • consumers and increase purchases. Public relations activities including fashion shows,
  • sponsorships, and press releases help maintain a strong brand image. Personal selling occurs
  • in stores where employees assist customers with styling and product selection. Direct
  • marketing uses SMS, emails, and catalogues to send personalized information to customers.
  • Digital marketing through influencers, Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube has become a
  • major tool for brand promotion. Visual merchandising uses attractive window displays and
  • store layouts to encourage impulse buying. These methods help brands attract new customers
  • and retain existing ones.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
